claims.statement: Across every vendor-provided Data/Custom system independently verified against Blood Moon's real config so far (ItemDrop.txt, CustomBotTrader.txt, CustomBotFusion.txt, CustomBotBuffer.txt, CustomMonster.txt), the file is present with the correct/current column structure but every configured data row is commented out or Enabled=0 -- only CustomBotStore.txt (CLAIM-006/017) is an exception, with 1 genuinely active entry.
claims.sourceLocation: Data/Item/ItemDrop.txt, Data/Custom/CustomBotTrader.txt, CustomBotFusion.txt, CustomBotBuffer.txt, CustomMonster.txt -- all read directly this session
claims.notes: 5 independent files now show the same pattern (1 exception: CustomBotStore is live). At this sample size it looks like a genuine operational characteristic of how Blood Moon's administrator(s) adopt vendor updates -- files get copied in during an update but are rarely individually enabled/customized/activated unless there's a specific reason (as with the Store). Sample is still small (5 of 90 files in Data/Custom) and drawn non-randomly (files this sweep happened to have video sources for) -- NOT yet strong enough to claim this holds for all 90 files, but strong enough to flag as a real pattern worth testing further. IMPORTANT UPDATE (Phase 3, per explicit instruction not to over-generalize this finding): the pattern does NOT hold for the 3 custom event files checked in Phase 3 (CustomEventZombie.txt, CustomEventPandora.txt, CustomEventStopOrDie.txt) -- none of these files has an obvious per-entry Enabled flag at all (a structurally different config shape than the Bot/Monster family), and all three contain real, distinct, non-template operational values (schedules, rewards, coordinates), not placeholder demo data. This is PATTERN_OBSERVED for the specific Bot-family + ItemDrop.txt + CustomMonster.txt files checked so far -- explicitly NOT a general BLOODMOON_POLICY that custom features are typically disabled. Do not extend this pattern to event configs or any other file family without independently checking each one.

claims.statement: A GM-only panel (opened with the D key, visible only to accounts holding GameMaster.txt permission) provides one-click buttons to open nearly every custom event this sweep has catalogued: 10 town Arenas (index 0-9), Team vs Team, Russian Roulette, Absorption, Hide and Seek, Drop Event/Drop Npc, BBB, Battle Royale, Racer, the core castle-family events (Blood Castle/Devil Square/Illusion Temple/Chaos Castle), Invasion Manager (indices 0-27), Capture the Flag, a Guild-vs-Guild-adjacent option, a generic PvP-event option, and a raffle ('sorteio') option -- each button simply invokes the corresponding existing GM command rather than adding new event logic.

verificationTargets.path: Data/Util/GetMyInfo (Custom Command Window flag) and Data/Command/ (OpenEvent command list)

claims.notes: High corroborating value: independently cross-references nearly every custom-event entity this sweep has already extracted (CustomEventZombie, Pandora, StopOrDie, PvpAll, and this Phase 5 batch's Auction/Racer/KillVsKill) as all being real, catalogued options in the vendor's own Season 6.18 GM tooling.

claims.statement: A separate player-facing panel (also opened with the D key, a 'Join Event' tab) lets any player join whichever event a GM currently has open without typing the /join command, and is enabled/visible via its own independent config flag, distinct from the GM panel's flag.

verificationTargets.path: Data/Util/GetMyInfo (Custom Command Window flag) and Data/Command/JoinEvent

claims.statement: The vendor's own GM-panel button roster for Invasion Manager (indices 0-27) is one index ahead of the real Season 6.18 InvasionManager.txt file the presenter cross-checked live on screen in this same video (which only goes up to index 26) -- an acknowledged, on-camera, unresolved off-by-one that the presenter explicitly noted ('falta uma aqui') but did not fix.
claims.notes: This is a claim about a vendor tooling bug/inconsistency, not a Blood Moon config fact -- recorded because it's directly relevant if any future work builds tooling that assumes the panel and the file are always in sync.

claims.statement: Update 8.1 adds a monster-model hover-preview (the cursor icon changes to show the tied monster's in-game appearance) plus a 2-field freeform text hint (e.g. a drop-chance callout like '20% chance to drop Bless/Soul') to each entry in the H-key event-schedule panel, both configured per-event in Data/Custom/CustomEventTime.txt.
claims.notes: Reinforces CLAIM-023's finding that the real vendor filename is CustomEventTime.txt (not 'CustomEventTimer') -- now confirmed by 2 independent video sources (lRhePn4cLZ0 and this video).

claims.statement: The monster-model hover-preview described in CLAIM-051 is not available for every monster on all engine versions -- the vendor states that on older versions ('6.3') only a limited early subset of monster models (up through Medusa) can be previewed this way.
claims.confidence: CONFIRMED_VENDOR_VIDEO (LOW -- exact version threshold garbled in the auto-caption audio)
claims.notes: Recorded as low-confidence and vendor-version-specific, not a Blood Moon fact -- the exact version number this refers to ('6.3', possibly a mis-transcription of a Season number) is uncertain and should not be relied on.

claims.statement: CustomMapRequirement (ADDED 8.0) lets an admin require players to hold specific item(s) and/or a currency amount (Cash/Gold/PcPoint/WCoin/GoblinPoint) before they can move to a configured map by /move command or the in-game map-teleport UI; on a successful move, the required item(s) and currency are automatically deducted from the player.
claims.notes: Demonstrated live with both an item check (a +15 Cristal, quantity 2) and a currency check (Cash/Gold/PcPoint) blocking movement until satisfied.

claims.statement: In CustomMapRequirement, setting an item's fields to an asterisk (*) disables that item's requirement check entirely (currency-only enforcement), and independently setting all currency amounts to 0 disables the currency requirement (item-only enforcement) -- the two requirement types are independently toggleable, and leaving both empty/zero disables the feature for that map entirely.

Update 7.9 adds a hover tooltip to the entry NPC/invitation of each of the 4 castle-family events (Blood Castle, Devil Square, Illusion Temple, Chaos Castle) that displays the configured reset/master-reset entry requirement range (the ResetMin/ResetMax mechanism, see CLAIM-035) and the event's configured prize -- but the tooltip only appears when the underlying reset-requirement is enabled for that specific event.
claims.notes: Direct extension of PROG-002/CLAIM-035's ResetMin/ResetMax mechanism -- this is a UI/visibility layer on top of an already-FACT-tier progression mechanic, not a new mechanic itself.

claims.statement: Unlike Blood Castle, Devil Square, and Illusion Temple (which use a dedicated map NPC for entry), Chaos Castle has no entry NPC -- its CLAIM-055 requirement tooltip is instead attached directly to the Chaos Castle invitation item itself, and the player must re-examine (hover/right-click) the invitation item to refresh the displayed requirement after a config change.
claims.notes: A vendor engine-architecture fact (why Chaos Castle behaves differently), not itself a Blood-Moon-specific config claim.

claims.statement: Update 7.7 adds a ground-item hover tooltip (item name + description) shown when the mouse passes over a dropped item, with no on/off config toggle at time of release (the presenter states a toggle was requested and planned for a future update). This is the base feature that a later video (CLAIM-012 / KI-005, ADDED 7.8) adds a Custom Info Drop Switch on/off toggle for.
claims.notes: Establishes the correct chronology: base tooltip shipped fixed-on at 7.7, the on/off switch (CLAIM-012) followed at 7.8.

claims.statement: Update 7.7 adds an on-screen FPS and MS(ping) monitor overlay, each independently toggleable via 2 separate flags in Data/Util/GetMyInfo, rendered as small corner text.

A related 'Custom Limit FPS' feature (raising the effective client FPS/movement speed) was shipped disabled by the vendor at 7.7's release because increasing movement speed this way can be misidentified by the engine's own anti-cheat system as a speed-hack.
claims.notes: A vendor-side known-bug disclosure, not a Blood Moon fact -- worth keeping because it explains why this specific flag might legitimately stay off in any real deployment.

claims.statement: Update 7.7 adds a D-key 'Custom Command Window' quick-action panel (toggled in GetMyInfo) with one-click buttons for the most common player self-service commands: class evolution, reset, master reset, clear inventory, clear skill, clear master skill, redistribute stat points, toggle PvP, add-point-to-Life, add-point-to-PvP-Life, clear PK status, and join events.
claims.notes: This is an earlier, player-only version of the same D-key panel concept later expanded with a GM-only Join/Open Event tab (CLAIM-048/049, ADDED 8.2).

claims.statement: Update 7.7 adds a character-info hover display mode ('type 2') that, unlike the default mode ('type 1', full stat build), shows only level/reset/master-reset/kills/deaths/free-or-VIP-status/class when hovering another player -- added specifically for 'hard build' servers that don't want a player's stat allocation visible to others.

CustomEventEntryLevel (ADDED 7.7) lets the admin configure a custom min/max character level to enter each of 5 events (Blood Castle, Devil Square, Chaos Castle, Kalima, Illusion Temple), replacing the engine's original hardcoded level ranges; the setting must be duplicated in both a server-side config file and a matching client-side file, and an asterisk (server-side max) does NOT translate directly -- the client-side file requires an explicit numeric max instead.

verificationTargets.path: Data/Custom/ (exact CustomEventEntryLevel filename unconfirmed) and its client-side counterpart

claims.notes: The video explicitly warns against blindly copying the server file's asterisk convention into the client-side file -- a real operational pitfall, not a hypothetical.

claims.statement: CustomEventEntryLevel includes a separate, lower 'special min level' specifically for MG and Dark Lord class characters, reflecting the vendor's stated convention that those 2 classes traditionally receive an entry-level discount relative to other classes for castle-family events.
claims.notes: A stated vendor convention/default, not itself a Blood-Moon-specific fact -- whether Blood Moon keeps this MG/DL discount is unverified.

claims.statement: The 'pega-pega' (tag/catch) event -- catalogued in this sweep as EVENT-run-and-catch -- cosmetically re-skins each participant to a configured monster-class appearance (a numeric index into CustomMonster.txt/Monster.txt, -1 = no change) upon joining, specifically so other players sharing the same public map can visually distinguish event participants from non-participants.
claims.notes: Demonstrated live using skin index 55 (Skeleton, per this sweep's own CustomMonster.txt cross-reference elsewhere in the corpus).

claims.statement: Renaming a custom event's GM-open command string (in Data/Command/OpenEvent) without also updating the matching prompt text in the language/Messenger file produces a player-facing inconsistency: the in-game message tells players to type the OLD command name while the server now only recognizes the NEW one.
claims.notes: An operator-safety/configuration-pitfall claim, not a verifiable Blood Moon fact -- but directly relevant to anyone renaming event commands.

claims.statement: The reworked CustomMonster/CustomNPC system (ADDED 7.2) supports 5 distinct client-side 'Type' visual modes for a custom entity: 0=NPC using a stock NPC-folder BMD model, 1=Monster using a stock Monster-folder BMD model, 2='Golden Monster' variant, 3=NPC assembled entirely from a 7-slot equippable item-set instead of a dedicated BMD model file, 4=Monster assembled the same equipment-set way.

verificationTargets.path: Data/Custom/CustomMonster.txt -- the Type field's meaning was not decoded when this file was read directly earlier in this sweep (CLAIM-020)

claims.notes: Worth a follow-up real-config check: CLAIM-020's real read of Blood Moon's CustomMonster.txt found all 7 configured entries commented out, so which Type value (if any) Blood Moon intended to use is currently unknown.

claims.statement: The item-set-based NPC/Monster appearance (Type 3/4, see CLAIM-066) uses a fixed 8-slot layout (0=Helm, 1=Armor, 2=Pants, 3=Gloves, 4=Boots, 5=Weapon1, 6=Weapon2/Shield, 7=Wings), each slot independently able to reference any real in-game item index/category and independently settable to Excellent quality; as of this video there is no Pet slot in this system, explicitly noted by the vendor as a possible future addition, not yet built.
claims.notes: The video's own slot count is stated as '0 to 7' (8 slots) despite the presenter saying 'sete itens' (seven items) colloquially -- the claim uses the literal enumerated slot list (8 slots, indices 0-7) rather than the spoken summary number.

claims.statement: A custom NPC configured with a shop (via a Shop Manager index plus a matching individual shop file) will fail to open its shop in-game unless the map number and X/Y coordinates in the shop config exactly match the coordinates configured for that same NPC in the monster/NPC placement file (MonsterSetBase.txt).
claims.notes: Stated explicitly and emphatically in the video ('se tiver diferente nao abre') -- a concrete, testable operational constraint.

claims.statement: Applying a new custom monster/NPC with a shop requires reloading 4 subsystems in this specific order for all changes to take effect: reload custom, reload monster, reload shop, reload skill.
claims.notes: An operational sequencing fact matching the 4 files touched earlier in the same video (Data/Custom/CustomMonster.txt's enable flag, MonsterSetBase.txt, the shop config, CustomMonsterSkill.txt).

claims.statement: CustomGuildVsGuild (rewritten UPDATED 6.9) is a throne-capture event: a 'crown' NPC spawns automatically at event start (and despawns at event end) at a configured map/coordinate; a guild member clicks it to claim the throne, and rival guild members must kill the current holder and click the NPC themselves to steal it. The winning guild (by total hold time/score) receives a guild-wide reward, and a separate top-5 individual ranking receives its own reward.
claims.notes: Demonstrated live end-to-end: throne captured, rival attempt blocked (rival wasn't registered in the event), event ended, rewards distributed, NPC despawned.

claims.statement: CustomGuildVsGuild requires a minimum guild-member count (admin-configured) to be eligible to participate, and -- new in update 6.9 -- supports a 'zone block' (map + coordinate rectangle) that physically prevents players from crossing into the event area until the event officially starts, automatically unlocking at the configured start time.
claims.notes: The zone-block was demonstrated live: a registered player was physically unable to cross the gate before the event officially started, then could pass the instant it opened.

claims.statement: Configuring CustomGuildVsGuild's entry NPC requires adding matching map/coordinate entries in 3 separate places that must all agree: the CustomGuildVsGuild config file itself, the monster/NPC placement file (MonsterSetBase.txt), and a separate NPC-type command-routing config (referred to in the video as 'NPC Viaturas' / Custom NPC) -- a mismatch in any one breaks the NPC's function.
claims.notes: The exact name 'NPC Viaturas' is an ASR rendering of an uncertain real term (possibly a mis-transcription) -- the underlying claim (3-way coordinate consistency requirement) is stated with confidence, the exact 3rd file's name is not.

claims.statement: Update 6.7 demonstrates CustomMonster.txt's Reset/Master-Reset reward columns working live: killing a specifically configured custom monster instance directly increments the killer's Reset and Master Reset counts (not merely a display value), confirmed on screen via a before/after character-info comparison.
claims.confidence: CONFIRMED_VENDOR_VIDEO (MEDIUM -- audio quality in this specific video is degraded, exact before/after numbers are not reproduced here)
claims.notes: Extends CLAIM-020's real-config finding (RewardLevel/RewardPoints columns exist on Blood Moon's CustomMonster.txt but all entries are disabled) with independent confirmation that the underlying reward mechanism genuinely works when enabled, per the vendor's own live demo.

claims.statement: In CustomMonster.txt's reward configuration, leaving a reward-currency field at -1 causes the in-game kill-reward message to display a literal '-1' value as a cosmetic bug; the vendor recommends using 0 instead to cleanly indicate 'no reward of that type' for a given monster.
claims.notes: A vendor-disclosed cosmetic bug/workaround, not itself a Blood Moon fact.

claims.statement: CustomEventPvP1x1 (ADDED 6.6) is a GM-curated single-duel event, distinct from the automated bracket tournament CustomEventKillVsKill (CLAIM-045): the GM selects exactly 2 specific players via a trade-window-style picker, sets a best-of-N kill count (Max Score) and an event duration, and only the eventual winner receives the configured 3-currency prize.
claims.notes: Participants are auto-PK-flagged (able to attack each other) on entry, matching the same pattern as other PvP-type custom events in this sweep.

claims.statement: Update 6.6 adds 2 new event entries to the H-key event-schedule panel (index 4=Crywolf, index 5=a Castle-Siege-affiliated event) plus a new 'monster quantity' column applying to invasion-type entries; the Castle-Siege entry only appears in the panel when the viewing player is connected to the GameServerCS instance (or standing on the Crywolf map), because those 2 events are specific to that separate server instance rather than the main GameServer.

The H-key event panel only lists events/invasions that are currently enabled -- a disabled entry (demonstrated live: Custom Arena, turned off) is silently omitted from the list entirely rather than shown greyed-out, meaning panel absence is not reliable evidence a feature doesn't exist -- it may simply be off, or (for Castle-Siege/Crywolf specifically) the viewer may not be connected to the right server instance.
claims.notes: A methodological caution worth keeping for this sweep's own future verification work -- an absent H-panel entry on any future Blood Moon screenshot/observation would NOT by itself prove that event is unconfigured.

claims.statement: Update 6.5 adds an optional 'Type' parameter to the /make, /makeset, and /drop commands: Type 0 preserves the original verbose syntax requiring every item field to be typed explicitly (category, index, level, skill, luck, option value, excellent bitmask, ancient flag, harmony id/level, socket count, durability); Type 1 is a new shorthand requiring only the category+index (or just index for makeset), auto-generating the item at its maximum/full-option roll with no harmony, no ancient stat, and no socket, intended to speed up admin actions during live events.
claims.notes: Demonstrated live for all 3 commands (make, makeset, drop) with matching Type-0 vs Type-1 behavior each time.

claims.statement: The /join (participar) player command only works for a whitelisted subset of events; it explicitly does NOT work for CustomArena, Battle Royale, or DropNpc, which instead require the player to click a dedicated map NPC to enter.

The /openevent (Abrir evento) GM command's syntax depends on whether the target event supports multiple configured instances: multi-instance events (e.g. CustomArena, 10 slots indexed 0-9) require both an index number and a name string that must exactly match the event's registered command string; single-instance events (e.g. Roleta Russa) always use index 0 with just the name string.
claims.notes: Demonstrated live for both cases (CustomArena index 3 'Master vs Master', and Roleta Russa index 0).

claims.statement: CustomGuildMapMove (ADDED 6.3) lets an admin designate a specific map as exclusive to one named guild (e.g. as an event-victory reward) -- only members of that exact guild (not even allied guilds) can move to the map; anyone else's move attempt is rejected with an in-game message naming the map's current owning guild. Multiple maps can each be independently assigned to different guilds simultaneously.
claims.notes: Demonstrated live with 2 maps owned by 2 different guilds simultaneously; alliance membership was explicitly shown NOT to grant access, only exact guild membership.

claims.statement: The original 5.7 version of the H-key event panel is built from 2 separate config sections: an 'Invasion Manager' list (the engine's fixed original events plus up to 5 free custom slots at indices 9-13, whose names are looked up from the language/Messenger file by message-ID) and a separate 'Custom Arena' list (its own 0-9 index range); the available Custom Arena slot count varies by base engine season (fewer slots on Season 2/3 and pre-Season client 97d than on Season 4+).
claims.notes: This is the ORIGINAL version of the feature; later videos in this sweep (lRhePn4cLZ0/CLAIM-023, KTO4Zk_Qxt8/CLAIM-051, lWclobV5zm8/CLAIM-076) describe subsequent updates to the same underlying panel.

claims.statement: Any edit to the H-key event panel's config requires regenerating the client-side .mpg file (via GetMyInfo) and copying it into the client folder before the changes take visible effect in-game -- the same GetMyInfo -> mpg -> client-copy workflow this sweep has observed for several other GetMyInfo-driven features (e.g. CLAIM-060/061).
claims.notes: A general vendor-engine operational workflow fact, applicable across many GetMyInfo-driven client features, not specific to this one event.

claims.statement: CustomMonsterSkill.txt lets an admin assign an attack-skill visual effect (from the client's own skill/magic ID list) to any monster class -- including custom-added monsters -- so the monster's attack animation displays that skill's visual effect (e.g. an elemental spell) instead of the engine's default melee/ranged animation.
claims.notes: Demonstrated live with 2 different monster instances simultaneously using visibly different assigned skill effects (an ice-family and a hell-fire-family visual). This is the same file referenced structurally in CLAIM-069's reload-order finding from a later (7.2) video.

claims.statement: CustomCaptureTheFlag (ADDED 5.4) awards a point to a team in exactly 2 ways: (a) a member returns the enemy team's stolen flag to their own team's designated NPC, or (b) a member kills an enemy player who is currently carrying their team's own stolen flag (which simultaneously returns the flag and scores the point) -- killing a non-flag-carrying opponent never scores a point.
claims.notes: Demonstrated live for both scoring paths.

claims.statement: In CustomCaptureTheFlag, dying while carrying the enemy's stolen flag causes the flag to be dropped/returned to its origin point, requiring another player to steal it again; team assignment (Red/Blue) on event entry is fully automatic/random with no player choice, and a tied score at the event's time limit results in no declared winner.
claims.notes: The tie-with-no-winner outcome was demonstrated live (2-2 score at time limit).

claims.statement: CustomEventRobber (ADDED 4.7) spawns a monster that steals either just the randomly-targeted victim's inventory items, or their entire loadout (equipped gear + inventory + wings + pet), per 2 independently toggleable config scopes; only the targeted victim can damage this specific monster instance, and killing it returns 100% of the stolen items plus some bonus loot the monster itself drops.
claims.notes: Demonstrated live end-to-end: monster spawned (MonsterClass 459, per the video's own on-screen text), stole the target's items, was killed by the target, items + bonus drop recovered.

claims.statement: CustomEventRobber supports 2 relevant targeting configurations: a general random-victim pool restricted to characters meeting a minimum Reset/Master-Reset/status-stat threshold (each independently disabled via -1), or a 'PK-only' mode that restricts the random-victim pool to currently PK-flagged players standing in open-PvP areas, excluding anyone inside a safe town.
claims.notes: The vendor states this PK-only mode was specifically designed to give a countermeasure against players who camp/grief in open-PvP zones ('pecar chato').

claims.statement: If CustomEventRobber's targeted victim disconnects before recovering their items, the monster despawns and the stolen items are automatically returned to the player -- an explicit no-item-loss guarantee even on disconnect.

CustomEventOnClick ('Evento Veloz'/quick-click) spawns a single NPC at a scheduled time; the first player to click it wins a combination of item (via a linked EventItemBag entry), currency, and/or VIP time, and subsequent clicks by other players after the prize is claimed yield nothing, with the winner's name broadcast server-wide.
claims.notes: Demonstrated live end-to-end: NPC spawned on schedule, clicked once, item+coins+VIP day awarded and confirmed via before/after VIP-expiry-date comparison.

claims.statement: CustomEventOnClick's VIP-time reward is configured independently for free vs. already-VIP players (distinct tier and day-count fields for each), specifically so a player who already holds a higher VIP tier isn't accidentally downgraded by winning a lower-tier VIP reward from the event.
